agent-planning.title: Agents plan multi-step work badly — they loop, stall, or skip steps
agent-planning.summary:
Give an agent a goal that takes ten steps and it will often take the wrong
ones: charge ahead on an ambiguous request instead of asking, follow a plan
that drifts, get stuck in a retry loop, or skip a step it needed. Planning,
turning a goal into the right ordered actions and knowing when to stop or ask,
is a distinct failure mode from tool use or memory.

sections.heading: TL;DR
sections.html: Give an agent a goal that takes ten steps and it will often take the wrong ones: charge ahead on an ambiguous request instead of asking, follow a plan that drifts, get stuck in a retry loop, or skip a step it needed. Planning, turning a goal into the right ordered actions and knowing when to stop or ask, is a distinct failure mode from tool use or memory.

sections.heading: State of the art
sections.html:
Robust planning comes from structure around the loop, not a better prompt. The ReAct loop (reason, act, observe, repeat) is the shared base, and the field now treats it as engineered infrastructure: framework APIs with persisted state and detached turns, portable loop libraries, and hooks that change an agent's tools mid-run. LangGraph, GitHub, and OpenAI describe the same practice under different names: graph, loop, or harness engineering.

Three refinements sit on top of the loop:

  • Decide before committing. Ask for clarification on vague goals, explore when the path is unclear, estimate how much work a task needs, and set reasoning effort per step. Scope estimation alone cut cost 85% at equal success in one benchmark.
  • Verify, then revise. Bounded worker/critic pairs, rubric graders with an iteration cap, and tests that guide implementation replace open-ended retry. Diagnosing why a step failed, across several hypotheses, is itself a planning step.
  • Learn the plan. Hindsight experience, RL on real tool interactions, and agents that write plans as reusable code all beat re-deriving a plan cold. Coding agents' synthesized planners outperformed hand-engineered ones.

How the harness carries state between steps matters as much as the model. Retaining reasoning and enabling compaction roughly tripled one model's ARC-AGI-3 score.

The open problem is measurement. Self-improving loops are only as good as their evaluator, and an end-to-end pass/fail cannot tell whether the agent or the loop failed. Benchmarks that score the loop controller separately and test procedures hundreds of pages long are first steps; production teams still lean on humans for most planning decisions.

sections.heading: Why it matters for platform engineers
sections.html: Bad planning turns a capable model into an unreliable agent. It causes runaway loops (a cost problem), confidently wrong work on ambiguous tickets, and the long-horizon failures that erode trust. The job is to wrap the model in a controllable harness: bounded loops, explicit decomposition, clarification checkpoints, verification, and re-planning on failure. Prove it with trajectory-level eval rather than hoping a bigger model plans better. Planning sits upstream of orchestration: once you can decompose reliably, the question becomes who executes each step.

themes.title: The agent loop as reusable infrastructure
themes.summary: The reason-act-observe loop is now packaged as frameworks, portable libraries, and production harnesses; vendors agree that structure around the loop, not a cleverer prompt, keeps multi-step runs on track.

themes.title: Deciding when to ask, explore, or how much to do
themes.summary: Clarification benchmarks, uncertainty signals, live state models, scope estimation, and reasoning-effort dials give a harness explicit moves before it commits to a plan.

themes.title: Verification loops and re-planning on failure
themes.summary: Bounded worker/critic pairs, rubric graders with iteration caps, test-anchored coding, and multi-hypothesis failure diagnosis replace blind retry with an explicit check-then-revise step.

themes.title: Learning to plan from experience, RL, and code
themes.summary: Agents improve plans with hindsight experience, RL on real tool interactions, evolvable harnesses, and plans written as reusable code; the evaluation signal remains the limiting factor.

themes.title: Benchmarks for loops and long-horizon procedures
themes.summary: New benchmarks score the loop controller separately from the agent, test reasoning about the harness's own lifecycle, and stretch planning horizons to hundreds of pages of procedures.

entries.title: Coding agents write task-and-motion planners that beat hand-engineered ones (56-95% vs. 47%)
entries.html:
Claude Code (Opus 5) and Codex (GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Astra) were each given a task description, simulator access, and a fixed budget to synthesize a reusable planning program, which was then frozen and tested on unseen instances. Across 28 environments (980 programs, 98,000 episodes), all three beat hand-engineered planners: 56-95% mean success versus 47% on the 16 environments with a planner baseline.

As object counts grew, the agents' programs kept their edge with an order of magnitude less computation per instance. Letting an agent write the plan as code generalizes better and cheaper than re-planning each episode.

evidence.title: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems

entries.title: TAM tests long-horizon procedure-following across hundreds of pages of manuals
entries.html:
Most multi-hop benchmarks are short-horizon, needing only a few retrieval or inference steps. Tasks over Application Manuals (TAM) tests whether a model can follow real procedures spanning hundreds of pages of interdependent guidelines, and finds gaps that short benchmarks miss.

It tests whether a plan stays consistent with a long manual, not a small task graph; related long-horizon gaps are tracked on agent evaluation.

evidence.title: Tasks over Application Manuals: Revealing Gaps in Long-Horizon Procedural Reasoning for Language Models

entries.title: LoopArena scores the loop's guidance separately from the coding agent's capability
entries.html:
In loop engineering, a controller monitors progress, assigns work, runs checks, and decides what the agent does next. LoopArena benchmarks models in that controller role: whether the loop trusts a stale progress note, skips verification, or stops before the task is safe to submit.

A single end-to-end pass/fail cannot tell whether the agent or the loop caused the outcome. LoopArena separates them.

evidence.title: LoopArena: Benchmarking Models as Runtime Controllers for Loop Engineering

entries.title: Keel pitches a conductor for coding agents that prove their work, not an agent loop
entries.html:
Keel (release 0.10) bills itself as "a conductor, not an agent loop" for AI coding agents that prove their work.

It is an explicit alternative to the loop-as-primitive framing most harnesses assume: an orchestrator that directs agents and checks evidence, rather than one open loop. The Show HN post gives no measured results.

evidence.title: Show HN: AI coding agents that prove their work

entries.title: GitHub's podcast decodes loops, harnesses, squads, and hill climbing for developers
entries.html:
The GitHub Podcast devotes an episode to the new vocabulary in developer conversations: loop engineering, harnesses, squads, hill climbing, and open weights.

The loop-engineering vocabulary has spread from research and conference circles into mainstream developer media.

evidence.title: Decoding the new AI lingo: Loops, harnesses, squads, hill climbing… oh my!

entries.title: CordisBench tests whether models can reason about a dynamic harness's component lifecycle
entries.html:
Dynamic harnesses let a model change the software that shapes its own execution, so a local plugin change can propagate through dependencies and cleanup. CordisBench is a 1,200-question benchmark of that lifecycle reasoning, combining a controlled formal setting with real programs.

The harness's own state becomes something the model has to reason about, not just run inside.

evidence.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?

entries.title: Deep Agents RubricMiddleware adds a grade-then-revise cycle with an iteration cap
entries.html:
LangChain's RubricMiddleware for Deep Agents turns a newline-delimited checklist of success criteria into a grade-then-revise cycle. A grader sub-agent with its own model, prompt, and optional tools checks the output, injects per-criterion feedback on failure, and the agent revises until it passes or hits a max-iteration cap.

Verification as a planning step ships as reusable middleware rather than a bespoke harness. The grader side is covered on LLM-as-judge.

evidence.title: Introducing Rubrics: Build Agents that Evaluate and Correct Their Work

entries.title: The /wayfinder skill gives agents an explicit explore-before-planning move
entries.html:
Matt Pocock's /wayfinder skill is for greenfield projects or work where the way forward is unclear. It treats planning as navigating a "fog of war": explore first, then commit to a plan.

It adds a third option beside asking for clarification and proceeding: scout the territory when decomposition is not obvious up front.

evidence.title: The /wayfinder Skill: Navigating the “Fog of War” of Planning

entries.title: TDD-Agent anchors a coding agent's plan to tests written as it reasons
entries.html:
Existing approaches use generated tests as static post-hoc validators, which limits their effect and can mislead when the tests are wrong. TDD-Agent uses test-driven reasoning so tests guide implementation during repository-level code generation.

The plan stays anchored to passing tests rather than a plausible-looking diff.

evidence.title: TDD-Agent: Test-Driven Reasoning for Code Generation

entries.title: Cloudflare cut Astro's GitHub issue load 85% by wrapping agents around triage
entries.html:
Per InfoQ, Cloudflare cut GitHub issue-triage work on the Astro project 85% with AI agents built into the workflow via GitHub Actions, Cloudflare Workers, and Flue, with humans kept in the loop.

It is a measured production case for wrapping a structured workflow around the model rather than routing raw model calls at each issue.

evidence.title: Cloudflare Cuts Astro GitHub Issues by 85% with AI Agents

entries.title: Netflix open-sources an actor-critic agent workflow for causal inference
entries.html:
Netflix open-sourced an agentic workflow for observational causal inference. Given observational data and the analyst's own plan, an actor-critic loop estimates causality, writes a report, and suggests next steps, reducing analysis toil.

The worker/critic structure from coding agents carries over to a data-science task, with the human supplying the plan the agent executes against.

evidence.title: Netflix Open-Sources Agentic Workflow for Causal Inference

entries.title: Krystal Loop Protocol bounds a coding agent's loop as a worker/critic pair
entries.html:
The Krystal Loop Protocol structures a coding agent's loop as a bounded worker/critic pair: one role proposes work, a second checks it, within an explicit bound rather than an open-ended retry.

It packages the propose-then-check structure as a named, reusable protocol instead of a bespoke harness detail.

evidence.title: Krystal Loop Protocol – a bounded worker/critic loop for AI coding agents

entries.title: Flue's React-style hooks let an agent attach tools and subagents mid-run
entries.html:
Astro creator Fred Schott's Flue 2 borrows React's hooks: useSkill(), useTool(), useSubagent(), and custom hooks among 16 built-ins, so tools, resources, and state can attach or change during a run instead of being fixed in config up front.

His framing names the planning gap: a support or triage bot "can't be fully configured in advance... it has to adapt in real-time." The harness is the foundation, not an afterthought, which gives a concrete mechanism for re-planning mid-run.

evidence.title: React for Agents: Astro Creator Brings Hooks to his Meta-Harness, Flue

entries.title: ChatGPT tunes its agent loop across harness, API, and inference together
entries.html:
A look at how ChatGPT optimizes its own agent loop treats the harness, the API, and inference as one system to tune together.

It is the loop-as-infrastructure view seen from inside a shipping consumer product rather than a framework or a paper.

evidence.title: ChatGPT Optimizes Its Agent Loop: Harness, API, and Inference

entries.title: Retaining reasoning and enabling compaction roughly tripled GPT-5.6's ARC-AGI-3 score
entries.html:
OpenAI reports that two API settings, retaining reasoning state across steps and enabling context compaction, together roughly tripled GPT-5.6's ARC-AGI-3 score and improved efficiency.

How the harness carries state between planning steps is itself a planning lever, not just which model runs them. The eval framing is on agent evaluation.

evidence.title: How enabling two settings tripled our scores on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark

entries.title: GitHub's Copilot team: build discipline around a stable harness, not each new tool
entries.html:
GitHub's "The harness is all you need (mostly)" lays out a repeatable Copilot workflow (prototype, plan, implement, review) and argues for building discipline around it instead of re-architecting every time a new AI tool ships.

A second major coding-agent vendor backs the loop-as-infrastructure view: harness stability is worth more than chasing novelty.

evidence.title: The harness is all you need (mostly)

entries.title: PoTRE splits reasoning across four specialized agents and tops Humanity's Last Exam
entries.html:
PoTRE (Poly-Topological Reasoning Ensembles) runs four heterogeneous agents (adversarial refinement, hierarchical strategic planning, spectrum search, direct chain) and reconciles them through a task-adaptive aggregation layer using candidate selection, semantic synthesis, or neuro-symbolic verification.

It reaches 49.92% on Humanity's Last Exam, above the previous best official score, with similar or fewer inference tokens than scaled single-stream baselines. Decomposing long-horizon reasoning across specialized roles can beat scaling one reasoner at comparable cost; see multi-agent.

evidence.title: PoTRE: Test-Time Reasoning inspired by Cognitive Heterogeneity

entries.title: Anthropic shows how to turn manual checks into Claude Code verification skills
entries.html:
Anthropic's guide shows how to turn a developer's own manual checks (does it compile, does it match the spec, did the test pass) into reusable skills, so Claude runs the verification step and closes its own feedback loop.

Verification becomes a packaged, repeatable step of the plan instead of a human re-checking every output.

evidence.title: Building verification loops in Claude Code with skills | Claude by Anthropic

entries.title: LangGraph: graph, loop, and harness engineering are one idea under three names
entries.html:
LangChain's three-year LangGraph retrospective argues graph engineering, loop engineering, and harness engineering are the same practice: placing model reasoning inside an explicit, inspectable control structure, with the right context at each step.

The convergence is industry-wide, not one vendor's pattern. Pick the control structure deliberately rather than trusting a single prompt to plan.

evidence.title: 3 Years of Graph Engineering with LangGraph

entries.title: Survey: agentic systems reach production by adding structure, not only stronger models
entries.html:
"Agents in the Wild" surveys agentic systems moving from research prototypes to production in software engineering, scientific discovery, and finance. It contrasts academic benchmark focus with deployment needs.

The deployment evidence backs the structure-around-the-loop thesis: decomposition, checkpoints, and guardrails carry production systems, not a stronger model alone.

evidence.title: Agents in the Wild: Where Research Meets Deployment

entries.title: Low/medium/high reasoning-effort modes give a harness a per-step deliberation knob
entries.html:
Sebastian Raschka explains how LLMs learn low, medium, and high reasoning-effort modes, which providers now expose to trade latency and cost for deliberation depth.

A harness can set "how hard should the model think before acting here" per step, instead of applying one fixed reasoning budget to every step of a plan.

evidence.title: Controlling Reasoning Effort in LLMs

entries.title: E3 estimates task scope before executing and cuts cost 85% at equal success
entries.html:
Agents often follow a maximum-context-first strategy, turning a one-line edit into a codebase audit. E3 (Estimate, Execute, Expand) estimates a minimal operating point, executes a minimum-sufficient path, and expands scope only when verification fails.

On a 121-edit benchmark it matches the strongest baseline's 100% success while cutting cost 85%, tokens 91%, and files inspected 92%. A live gpt-4o harness showed milder but real over-reading. Deciding how much work a task needs before executing is the cheapest fix for over-scoped plans.

evidence.title: Do AI Agents Know When a Task Is Simple? Toward Complexity-Aware Reasoning and Execution

entries.title: Google's Genkit Agents API packages the loop, with detached turns and interruptible tools
entries.html:
Google released the Genkit Agents API in preview for TypeScript and Go. It packages message history, the tool-call loop, streaming, and state persistence behind one chat() interface.

Two primitives matter for planning. Detached turns let an agent keep working after the client disconnects. Interruptible tools add human-in-the-loop approval mid-plan, with anti-forgery validation on resume. "Ask vs. proceed" gets a framework-level mechanism instead of a bespoke one.

evidence.title: Google's Genkit Ships Agents API with Detached Turns and Human-in-the-Loop for TypeScript and Go

entries.title: Lilian Weng maps ~35 papers on harness engineering for self-improvement
entries.html:
Lilian Weng's survey names three recurring harness patterns: goal-oriented plan, execute, observe, improve loops; the file system as persistent memory; and parent agents spawning inspectable sub-agents. It goes further by treating the harness code itself as an artifact an LLM mutation operator can evolve (AlphaEvolve, Darwin Gödel Machine).

Her caveat matters as much as the taxonomy: self-improvement loops are only as good as their evaluation signal, and weak evaluators remain the bottleneck. Pair any harness-evolution experiment with trajectory-level eval.

evidence.title: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement
[AINews] Lilian Weng summarizes 35 papers on Harness Engineering for RSI

entries.title: AWS's multi-turn RL checklist: trusted environment, external eval, task-aligned reward
entries.html:
AWS's best practices for multi-turn RL in SageMaker AI list the operational steps for training agents on long interactions:

  • build a training environment you can trust
  • run an external evaluation separate from the reward signal
  • design the reward to match the end task
  • manage what changes once the agent runs for multiple turns
  • monitor the metrics that tell you when to iterate

It is the checklist underneath "just fine-tune on tool interactions".

evidence.title: Best practices for multi-turn reinforcement learning in Amazon SageMaker AI

entries.title: Research agents recover better by weighing several failure hypotheses than by one reflection
entries.html:
Autonomous research agents usually recover from a failed experiment with a single free-form reflection that compresses metrics, logs, and design choices into one critique. This work generates several candidate explanations for the failure, weighs them, and re-plans around the most likely cause.

Failure diagnosis becomes a planning step, not a trigger for blind retry.

evidence.title: One Reflection Is Not Enough: Self-Correcting Autonomous Research via Multi-Hypothesis Failure Attribution

entries.title: Candidly's per-turn state model halved disengaging turns (23% to 11%)
entries.html:
Candidly built an IO-HMM over per-turn signals such as message length and semantic alignment. It infers whether a conversation is Engaged, Detailed, Guided, or Disengaging and steers the agent's next turn accordingly.

In production, disengaging turns fell from 23% to 11% and the Engaged state rose from 53% to 64%. Inferring mid-episode whether the plan is working, not just scoring the end result, was worth the extra model.

evidence.title: How Candidly Built State Aware Agent Harnesses With Langsmith

entries.title: Iterative, human-curated skill engineering beats one-shot AI design
entries.html:
Paul Bakaus, discussing his tool Impeccable, argues against one-shot AI design: iterative, human-curated task specs ("skills") get better plans than hoping a single prompt gets them right, even in a "loopmaxxing" era.

Treat task specs as artifacts you refine across runs, with human judgment in the loop.

evidence.title: Skill engineering and the case against one-shot AI design

entries.title: QUALITY.md proposes an open spec, skill, and CLI for grading loop engineering
entries.html:
QUALITY.md is an open format, agent skill, and CLI for holistic quality evaluation of a project. Its author found it suited loop engineering, and wants to move teams from a reactive review-and-repair mindset to defining quality up front.

It names harness quality as something to measure directly instead of leaving it implicit in end results.

evidence.title: Show HN: QUALITY.md – open format/specification, agent skill, and CLI

entries.title: A provider-agnostic agent loop built on ports and adapters
entries.html:
An engineer at Featherless kept rebuilding the same loop (call model, run tools, feed results back, stop), so he extracted it and put every piece behind an interface. The MIT-licensed result works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint and does not own the UI or control flow.

The loop itself becomes portable infrastructure, separable from any one framework or provider.

evidence.title: Show HN: A provider-agnostic agent loop built on ports and adapters

entries.title: CoMet decomposes multimodal uncertainty, the signal an agent needs to decide whether to ask
entries.html:
CoMet targets uncertainty estimation in multimodal models by decomposing what kind of uncertainty a model has, from context and from multiplicity of valid answers.

"Knowing what you don't know" is the input a planning loop needs to choose between asking a clarifying question and proceeding. CoMet works on producing that signal; benchmarks like DiscoBench only score the decision.

evidence.title: CoMet: Context and Multiplicity Decomposition for Multimodal Uncertainty Estimation

entries.title: Autoresearch has agents iterate on their own task recipes, with humans still steering
entries.html:
Introspection co-founder Roland Gavrilescu describes autoresearch: agents iterate on their own task recipes across runs, closing a feedback loop over the plan itself rather than over individual steps.

He is explicit that humans remain central to steering the loop. Self-improving plans still need someone choosing what "better" means.

evidence.title: Autoresearch: The feedback loop behind self-improving agents

entries.title: OpenAI's Agent RFT trains reasoning models on real tool interactions to fix credit assignment
entries.html:
Agent RFT fine-tunes reasoning models with reinforcement learning against real-time tool interactions and custom reward signals. The InfoQ talk frames it as solving credit assignment: which of many steps in a long trajectory caused success or failure.

Speakers report enterprise cases where it removed long-tail token loops. Training now targets planning directly, not only the harness around it.

evidence.title: Presentation: Fine Tuning the Enterprise: Reinforcement Learning in Practice

entries.title: Morph Reflexes flags looping and other behavioral failures from traces without a frontier judge
entries.html:
Morph Reflexes serves semantic signals from agent traces over an API, with classifier heads for looping, reasoning leakage, and user frustration. Its pitch: judging every turn with a frontier model is too slow and expensive at scale.

A planning loop that stalls or repeats needs a detector cheap enough to run on every turn. Classifier signals make "is the agent stuck" a runtime check instead of a post-mortem finding. Cost details are on LLM-as-judge.

evidence.title: Show HN: Morph Reflexes – Multi-head classifiers for agent traces

entries.title: Loops and software factories dominated the AI Engineer World's Fair
entries.html:
Latent Space's dispatch from the AI Engineer World's Fair reports that "loops" and "software factories", production setups that wrap a planning loop in enough infrastructure to run it repeatedly, were a dominant theme alongside forward-deployed engineering and open models.

Planning as a harness problem has moved from research framing into mainstream practitioner conversation.

evidence.title: AIEWF Daily Dispatch: Loops, Software Factories & Forward Deployed Engineers

entries.title: Stripe runs a ReAct compliance agent on a dedicated service with guardrails and human oversight
entries.html:
An AWS write-up of Stripe's financial-compliance agent describes a ReAct framework (reason, act, observe, repeat) running on a dedicated agent service, with guardrails, human oversight for accountability, and lessons on task decomposition.

The ReAct loop alone does not keep multi-step runs on track at production scale. Planning reliability is an architecture problem, solved with infrastructure around the loop, not a prompt problem.

evidence.title: Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe

entries.title: GUI agents that explore and reuse hindsight experience plan repetitive tasks better
entries.html:
Small open multimodal web agents are cheap and private but plan poorly and generalize weakly across websites. This work has them autonomously explore interfaces and reuse hindsight experience from earlier attempts, which improves task decomposition on repetitive GUI tasks over zero-shot planning.

A plan learned from prior runs beats one re-derived cold each time, which matters most when you want a small model instead of a frontier one.

evidence.title: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning

entries.title: DiscoBench scores whether search agents ask for clarification on vague goals
entries.html:
Most search-agent benchmarks assume the user's query is complete. DiscoBench measures clarification-aware deep search: whether an agent recognizes an under-specified goal and asks instead of confidently planning down the wrong path.

It treats "ask a question" as a first-class planning action that a harness should test for, not a sign of weakness.

evidence.title: When Search Agents Should Ask: DiscoBench for Clarification-Aware Deep Search

entries.title: DAIN adapts the agent collaboration structure to each task instead of a fixed plan
entries.html:
DAIN (Dynamic Agent-based Interaction Network) reframes multimodal fusion as a dynamic network of interacting agents whose collaboration and reasoning structure adapts per task, instead of a static mixture-of-experts routing.

The planning lesson: the structure of who reasons about what can itself be chosen per task rather than fixed up front.

evidence.title: DAIN: Dynamic Agent-Based Interaction Network for Efficient and Collaborative Multimodal Reasoning

agent-reliability.title: Agents give fluent, confident-looking output even when it's wrong
agent-reliability.summary:
An agent can hallucinate a fact, skip a step, or misuse a tool and still
return a fluent, confident-looking answer; nothing in the output signals that
it's wrong. Deciding where to trust the model versus a deterministic tool, and
making an agent prove its work rather than claim success, is a separate
engineering problem from measuring that work afterward (see
[agent evaluation](/topic/agent-evaluation)).

sections.heading: TL;DR
sections.html: An agent can hallucinate a fact, skip a step, or misuse a tool and still return a fluent, confident-looking answer; nothing in the output signals that it's wrong. Deciding where to trust the model versus a deterministic tool, and making an agent prove its work rather than claim success, is a separate engineering problem from measuring that work afterward (see agent evaluation).

sections.heading: State of the art
sections.html:
Reliability is a system property, not a model property. No current model stops hallucinating at scale, so the working answer is to contain errors with structure around the model rather than wait for a better one.

Four patterns carry most of the weight:

  • Deterministic boundaries. Constrained schemas, server-side gates that check a tool call before it is sent, compilers that reject invalid generated code, and harness invariants such as serialized state mutations. Enforcement lives outside the model's decision.
  • Durable execution. Checkpointing and exactly-once runtimes borrowed from distributed systems; Brex's move to Temporal took long-run completion from about 96% to 99.9%. Agent identity is the weaker leg: it still borrows workload-identity patterns that assume every replica behaves the same.
  • Layered hallucination control. Grounded generation, decoding-time calibration, calibrated detectors, and abstention, stacked as in the HALO architecture. Detection is precise in-domain but transfers poorly across domains.
  • Proof of work. Tooling that requires evidence of completion, plus user-flagged error signals from production, because false completion is a standard failure mode.

The measurement itself is shaky. A ReAct agent that passes 77% of runs on average passes all five runs only 53% of the time, and container resourcing alone moves coding scores by up to 6 points. Humans still make about 70% of planning decisions in Claude Code sessions, which props up reliability that fully unattended runs would not have.

The open problem is the verifier. Verification is now the bottleneck, and for agents that edit their own tools and harness, nobody has a verifier the agent cannot also rewrite. Diagnosis has the same gap: models read logs well but still confuse correlation with cause.

sections.heading: Why it matters for platform engineers
sections.html: Reliability spans three layers you build separately: an identity system that can scope and audit what an agent does, an execution substrate that survives crashes and rate limits without dropping work, and an intent check that catches an agent giving up or declaring victory early. A better model fixes none of them. Skip one and a confident agent can be wrong, stalled mid-task, or done without you knowing which. Budget for pass-every-time evals and action-time spend alerts, not just average accuracy and monthly billing reports. Scoped credentials are shared with sandboxing.

themes.title: Deterministic boundaries around the model
themes.summary: Production teams bound the model with schemas, server-side gates, type checkers, and harness invariants, so enforcement sits outside the model's own decision instead of inside a longer prompt.

themes.title: Agent identity, durable execution, and spend guards
themes.summary: Durable runtimes like Temporal deliver measured completion gains, while agent identity still borrows service-account patterns and cloud billing alerts lag agent-speed spend by about a day.

themes.title: Containing hallucination during and after generation
themes.summary: Hallucination is treated as a containable failure through layered oversight, decoding-time calibration, and calibrated detectors, with evidence that some hallucinations widen useful context rather than mislead.

themes.title: Proving the work instead of trusting "done"
themes.summary: The bottleneck has moved from generating output to verifying it; proof-of-work tooling, user-flagged errors, and verified-outcome training help, but the verifier is still the weak point for self-improving agents.

themes.title: Consistency, autonomy limits, and the human role
themes.summary: Average pass rates overstate reliability, infrastructure config moves scores by up to 6 points, and humans still make most planning decisions; autonomy is a cost to justify, not a default.

entries.title: Production agent failures come from the harness, and four invariants address them
entries.html:
OpenAI's Vinoth Govindarajan argues, using incidents such as OpenClaw, that production agents fail beyond model hallucination. He places the fix in the harness:

  • explicit state ownership
  • serialized concurrent state mutations, so two in-flight actions cannot corrupt shared state
  • execution authority scoped per step
  • actions validated at the user-visible edge, not by the model's own account of what it did

Each item is an invariant a team can audit its harness against.

evidence.title: Presentation: The Agent Harness: Control Planes, Invariants, and Approval Boundaries for Production AI Agents

entries.title: Typed Domain Grounding lets a host language's type checker catch invalid LLM-generated DSL code
entries.html:
Irakli Betchvaia's Typed Domain Grounding embeds a domain-specific language inside a mainstream typed language, so the host compiler and type checker, not a second LLM pass, reject invalid generated output. He evaluates it on kUML benchmarks and an infrastructure-as-code example with generate-compile-repair loops.

For code generation, the cheapest verifier is often a compiler you already have.

evidence.title: Article: Your Next DSL Author Is a Language Model

entries.title: With AI-generated code, the bottleneck has moved from generation to verification
entries.html:
Nitin Garg's InfoQ article on spec-driven development argues that as AI-generated code volume grows, it brings security weaknesses and familiar bug patterns, so the engineering cost shifts from writing code to detecting where generated behavior diverges from stated intent.

Plan review capacity around verification, with a spec as the reference point, rather than around generation speed.

evidence.title: Article: When Spec-Driven Development Pays Off

entries.title: DescaPE uses internal attribution signals to stop early factual errors from snowballing
entries.html:
DescaPE locates a factual-salient layer span inside the model with sliding-window MLP ablation and uses that internal signal during decoding to suppress hallucination-prone trajectories before early factual errors compound through autoregressive generation.

It brings the decoding-time containment approach from vision-language models to plain-text generation, where post-hoc correction arrives after the error has already propagated.

evidence.title: Look Before You Leap: Factual Decoding with Internal Attribution Signals

entries.title: A DeBERTa plus MC Dropout detector reaches F1 0.915 on HaluEval but transfers poorly across domains
entries.html:
A response-level detector combines fine-tuned DeBERTa-v3, Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty, and temperature-scaled calibration. On HaluEval it reaches F1 0.915 and AUROC 0.977, and MC Dropout inference lifts accuracy to 93.2%.

The caveat matters for production: general-domain training transfers poorly to the SciFact biomedical benchmark (F1 0.52), and domain-matched PubMedBERT only reaches F1 0.63. A cheap detector is precise enough to gate on in-domain, but each domain needs its own training.

evidence.title: Domain-Specific Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models

entries.title: A 77% average pass rate hides a 53% pass-every-time rate; episodic guidelines close part of the gap
entries.html:
On AppWorld, a ReAct agent on GPT-4.1 run five times on the same task succeeds on every run only 53% of the time, though its per-run pass rate averages 77%. The authors call the 24-point shortfall the consistency gap.

Their fix: a Consistency Analyzer flags the trajectory steps most likely to flip between runs, and a Guideline Generator writes a targeted guideline into episodic memory for similar future tasks. All-five-runs success rose 16 points on seen tasks and 13 points on unseen similar ones.

For unattended use, measure pass-every-time, not average pass rate. See agent memory for the storage side.

evidence.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course

entries.title: TASPO assigns per-action credit from verified runs and beats GRPO by 10.6%
entries.html:
Outcome-based agentic RL applies one verified success or failure signal to every step of a long trajectory. TASPO converts privileged supervision from verified successful runs into per-action credit weights that are positive, bounded, and mean-preserving, so the verified outcome still sets the update's direction and scale.

Across three agentic benchmarks it improves 10.6% over GRPO and generalizes better to unseen tasks. Some "confident but wrong" behavior traces back to how the policy was trained, not only to which checks run on its output.

evidence.title: Reconciling Process Supervision with Outcome-Based Credit in Agentic Policy Optimization

entries.title: Anthropic: start with one well-prompted call and add autonomy only when it pays
entries.html:
Anthropic's "Building Effective AI Agents" sets the default explicitly: start with the simplest solution that works, often a single well-prompted call, and move to a workflow or an autonomous agent only when the added complexity demonstrably improves outcomes.

Agentic autonomy is a cost to justify, not a default architecture.

evidence.title: Building Effective AI Agents

entries.title: Coding-agent autonomy hits a wall where small misjudgments compound
entries.html:
A practitioner critique argues coding-agent autonomy hits a wall past a certain task complexity. Longer unattended runs compound small misjudgments into a wrong trajectory faster than the model corrects them.

Bound how much unattended autonomy a task earns instead of extending run length by default.

evidence.title: The Wall Confronting Reliable Coding Agent Autonomy

entries.title: Container resourcing alone swings agentic coding scores by up to 6 points
entries.html:
Anthropic found that infrastructure configuration, container CPU/RAM allocation and how strictly it is enforced, can move agentic coding scores by up to 6 percentage points on Terminal-Bench 2.0.

That is enough noise to erase an apparent reliability gain. Pin and report the eval infrastructure alongside the model; methodology is on agent evaluation.

evidence.title: Quantifying infrastructure noise in agentic coding evals

entries.title: In 400,000 Claude Code sessions, people make 70% of planning calls but only 20% of execution calls
entries.html:
Anthropic's analysis of roughly 400,000 Claude Code sessions splits responsibility along the plan/execute line: people make about 70% of planning decisions but only 20% of execution decisions. Expert users trigger about twice the actions per prompt that novices do (12 vs. 5) and five times the output (3,200 vs. 600 words).

Reliability today leans on where humans still hold the pen, which is planning rather than unattended execution. Removing that human checkpoint removes part of the reliability you are currently getting for free.

evidence.title: How Claude Code is used in practice

also.title: Agents plan multi-step work badly — they loop, stall, or skip steps

entries.title: In incident response, Claude excels at reading logs and fails at causation
entries.html:
Anthropic reliability engineer Alex Palcuie reports on using Claude for incident response:

  • Observe works. It flagged 4,000 accounts created at once with identical traits as coordinated fraud, and root-caused a Rust panic in checkpoint.rs before engineers finished reading the logs.
  • Orient breaks. Seeing requests and errors double together, it repeatedly called a capacity problem when a failed KV cache was the cause; the engineer corrected it "six, seven times" before adding the distinction to the system prompt.
  • Postmortems come out "80% readable" but miss contributing factors.

The open risk: if AI runs mitigation, humans lose the feedback loop that builds senior-responder judgment.

evidence.title: Presentation: Can Claude Fix Itself? Using LLMs for Incident Response

entries.title: LLM selection systems stay reliable with constrained schemas and a discriminator check
entries.html:
In an InfoQ talk on LLM-powered selection systems, Jendrik Jördening restricts model output to a constrained schema, separates semantic extraction (where the model is needed) from the deterministic code that acts on it, and validates the model's choices with a discriminator model before they reach the database.

He structures the pipeline as an MVC-style split so non-determinism stays in one layer instead of leaking into storage and downstream logic.

evidence.title: Presentation: From Thousands to One: Building LLM-Powered Selection Systems

entries.title: Recursive self-improvement needs a verifier that rises with the agent
entries.html:
Phil Schmid notes that agents can already edit their own tools, skills, and harness. Recursive self-improvement still needs a system that can raise the verifier without the agent capturing it.

A self-modifying agent can also modify its own check. Any self-improvement loop needs a verifier the agent cannot rewrite.

evidence.title: Recursive Self-Improvement

entries.title: ReWEIGH calibrates visual evidence per token during decoding to cut VLM hallucination
entries.html:
ReWEIGH calibrates token-level ordinal visual evidence during decoding in vision-language models. It projects visual-token states through the output head to measure how strongly the image supports each candidate token, instead of only judging the finished output.

It is the "contain it during generation, not just catch it after" approach, applied inside the decoding step.

evidence.title: ReWEIGH the Evidence: Calibrating Token-Level Ordinal Visual Evidence to Mitigate Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models

entries.title: AutoResearch ties autonomous research insights back to experimental evidence
entries.html:
AutoResearch is a two-stage system that links idea generation to idea execution so autonomous research workflows stay scientifically grounded. Its premise, "insight in, hallucination out", is that automation alone does not keep a long research run rigorous.

For long-running agents, grounding has to be a design target of the workflow, checked through experiments, rather than assumed from automation.

evidence.title: AutoResearch: Insight In, Hallucination Out

entries.title: LangSmith's Perceived Error signal finds agent mistakes from what users flagged
entries.html:
LangSmith Tuned Evaluators attach quality feedback to production traces, starting with a Perceived Error signal that surfaces agent mistakes from user reactions in production.

It adds a user-facing check alongside independent judges and trace mining: the agent's "done" is tested against whether the user thought it was right. The eval-tooling side of the release is on agent evaluation.

evidence.title: Introducing LangSmith Tuned Evaluators

entries.title: Let the model hallucinate a label, then snap it to the real vocabulary with embeddings
entries.html:
Simon Willison describes Doug Turnbull's trick for tagging against a vocabulary too large for one prompt (his blog has 1,856 tags). Ask the model to output tags with no knowledge of the existing vocabulary, then use vector-embedding similarity to map each guess to the nearest real tag.

It swaps a task the model is bad at (choosing from thousands of options) for one it does well (free generation plus retrieval). It only works because the embedding step grounds the hallucination instead of returning it as-is.

evidence.title: Don't classify. Hallucinate!

entries.title: Brex moved onboarding agents to Temporal and long-run completion rose from ~96% to 99.9%
entries.html:
Brex routes production onboarding-agent workflows through Temporal Cloud instead of a bespoke retry loop. Long-running completion rose from roughly 96% to 99.9%, and the workflow code stayed unchanged because the durable runtime is swapped in underneath it.

Checkpoint recovery and exactly-once execution become infrastructure you buy, not logic you re-implement per agent. The same article covers running that code in-process for evals; see agent evaluation.

evidence.title: Article: Runtime-Agnostic AI Workflows: A Pattern for Production Durability and Fast Eval Iteration

entries.title: HALO treats hallucination as a containable failure with six layers of defense
entries.html:
HALO (Hallucination-Aware Layered Oversight) argues "zero hallucination" is a property a system enforces, not one a model has. It stacks six layers:

  • grounded generation over approved content
  • constrained, deterministic execution that bounds where the model can err
  • multi-signal verification: an LLM judge plus evidence checks against source text
  • calibrated abstention when grounding is thin
  • traceability of every retrieval, tool call, and generation
  • continuous oversight that detects drift and regenerates on threshold breaches

It puts the identity/execution/intent controls into one composable architecture instead of waiting for a model that does not hallucinate.

evidence.title: Zero Hallucination, by Construction: Hallucination-Aware Layered Oversight for Trustworthy Enterprise AI

entries.title: Agent-speed cloud spend outruns billing alerts that lag about a day
entries.html:
A three-person agency got a $14,000 AWS bill in one day after attackers extracted static access keys with unrestricted Bedrock access and burned them on Claude calls. In the DN42 incident, an autonomous agent with open-ended AWS access provisioned $6,531 of oversized infrastructure in 24 hours. A credit-card charge caught both, because Cost Explorer and Budgets work off data that lags roughly a day.

The fix is scoped credentials and action-time alerts applied to spend: IAM roles instead of static keys, service-control policies blocking expensive instance families, and CloudTrail alerts on RunInstances and InvokeModel.

evidence.title: AI Agents with Cloud Credentials Are Outrunning Billing Guardrails Built for Human-Speed Mistakes

entries.title: Server-side gates check a tool call after the model decides but before the request is sent
entries.html:
Quickchat's write-up on reliable agent actions describes two mechanisms. A server-side gate evaluates conditions after the model decides to call a tool but before the request goes out, so a prompt-injected model cannot talk its way past the check. A JSONPath extraction step stores values from earlier API responses so later steps reference a saved field instead of the model re-typing, and possibly hallucinating, an ID.

Enforcement lives outside the model's decision, not inside a longer, more careful prompt.

evidence.title: How to Make Your AI Agent's Actions Reliable (No Code)

entries.title: Grok 4.5 cuts coding-agent cost about 80% but raises the hallucination rate
entries.html:
Tech Times coverage puts Grok 4.5's coding-agent cost roughly 80% below a comparable frontier setup, at near-frontier speed and accuracy, but with the hallucination rate roughly doubling as accuracy rose. The figures are from press coverage, not an independent benchmark.

A cheaper, faster model is not a free swap. The saving only holds if the harness adds verification to catch the extra hallucinations; see agent cost for the cost side.

evidence.title: Grok 4.5 Cuts Coding-Agent Cost 80%: Near-Frontier Speed, Higher Hallucinations - Tech Times

entries.title: Sonn watches a coding session and nudges the agent before it repeats a settled mistake
entries.html:
Sonn is a persistent reasoning layer that watches a coding agent's session live and injects a nudge the moment a past decision becomes relevant again, such as a previously rejected approach or a settled architecture choice.

It moves reliability work upstream: from checking the output after the fact to steering the decision before the agent makes it. The claim comes from a Show HN launch, with no published accuracy numbers.

evidence.title: Show HN: Sonn a reasoning layer that nudges coding agent before it makes mistake

entries.title: Agent identity, reliable execution, and intent are each only half-solved
entries.html:
An essay splits agent reliability into three legs:

  • Identity has no purpose-built primitive. Platforms retrofit workload identity: SPIFFE-based identities (Gemini Enterprise), service principals plus token brokers (Microsoft Entra). The fit is poor because two runs of the same agent can behave differently.
  • Execution borrows the distributed-systems playbook: checkpoint recovery, exactly-once guarantees, cgroup quotas, per-session microVM or gVisor isolation.
  • Intent is least solved. Models drift from the task or report false completion. Fixes split between LLM-graded trajectory checks and cheaper encoder classifiers that score task completion, an auditability and cost trade-off.

The identity leg overlaps with sandboxing and scoped credentials.

evidence.title: Agent Identity, Reliable Execution, and Intent are only half-way solved

entries.title: Hallucinated captions can raise accuracy on vision-language tasks, HIVE finds
entries.html:
HIVE is an evaluation harness for post-hallucination reasoning: what happens after hallucinated content enters a vision-language model's context. Across nine tasks and nine models, hallucinated captions often improved accuracy on vision-language tasks by broadening semantic coverage, while text-only tasks showed limited or unstable effects.

"Does the agent hallucinate" is the wrong single-axis question. What matters is whether a given hallucination widens useful context or misleads the next reasoning step.

evidence.title: HIVE: Understanding Post-Hallucination Reasoning in Vision Language Models

entries.title: NVIDIA splits agent platforms into deterministic tools for certainty and agents for discovery
entries.html:
In an InfoQ talk, NVIDIA's Aaron Erickson describes purpose-built agent hierarchies that separate tools for certainty (deterministic code you can trust) from space for the model's own discovery. He pairs the split with LLM-as-judge test pyramids and warns against the paradox of choice: giving an agent too many options lowers reliability.

Deciding which parts of a task get deterministic treatment becomes an explicit architecture decision, made at design time, rather than something left to the model at run time.

evidence.title: Presentation: Designing AI Platforms for Reliability: Tools for Certainty, Agents for Discovery

entries.title: Coding-agent tooling that requires verifiable proof of completion, not a "done" claim
entries.html:
Make No Mistakes, a Show HN project, is built around one rule: an AI coding agent must prove its work with verifiable evidence of completion instead of the harness trusting the agent's own "done" signal.

It is a practitioner-side instance of the same idea the research work on this page converges on. False completion is a known failure mode, so the completion claim itself has to be checked.

evidence.title: Show HN: Make No Mistakes – AI coding agents must prove their work

grounding.title: An agent's answer is only as good as what it retrieved — and whether it can prove it
grounding.summary:
A fluent agent answer isn't the same as a grounded one: the model will answer
past what it actually retrieved unless the retrieval was current, the right
slice, and cheap enough to fetch — and unless something checks that the
answer is actually backed by what came back. Grounding is the retrieval and
attribution problem underneath [agent memory](/topic/agent-memory).

sections.heading: TL;DR
sections.html: A fluent agent answer isn't the same as a grounded one: the model will answer past what it actually retrieved unless the retrieval was current, the right slice, and cheap enough to fetch — and unless something checks that the answer is actually backed by what came back. Grounding is the retrieval and attribution problem underneath agent memory.

sections.heading: State of the art
sections.html:
Retrieval architecture is a per-job choice, not a default to embeddings. Production teams answer exact questions with plain SQL, use knowledge graphs for connected and provenance-heavy questions, and reserve vector search for the fuzzy slice. Gateways, self-hosted or managed, route across stores. The strongest production results credit a governed data layer underneath the agent, such as dbt and a semantic model, more than the retrieval method.

The retriever keeps improving under every architecture. Better text and multimodal embedders, structured extraction of charts, learned control of how much to search per query, and recovering a sufficient set of evidence rather than the top-ranked passages all raise recall without changing the store. Better retrieval also means fewer search calls, so it is a cost and latency lever.

What enters context is a budget. A raw web page can cost tens of thousands of tokens of boilerplate. Pre-compression, reusable compression views, and models hardened against distracting context all attack the same waste.

The open problem is evidence that is true but misleading. Reordered salience, true evidence for a nearby question, and poisoned embeddings that mimic benign entries all redirect agents without a single false claim or injected instruction. Published defenses cut attack success but do not transfer cleanly across datasets or attack types.

Attribution is becoming enforceable. Benchmarks score citation support, verifiers check per claim that an MCP agent cites the right source, runtime guards check actions against ground truth before they execute, and auditable domains split the decision (rules) from the explanation (RAG).

sections.heading: Why it matters for platform engineers
sections.html: Grounding is the trust layer underneath every agent answer that cites a source or claims a fact: get it wrong and the agent is fluent but unverifiable, which is worse than an obvious failure because users don't know to distrust it. The engineering job splits three ways — pick the retrieval architecture (vector, graph, SQL, or a gateway spanning all three; see vector-kb), budget the token cost of fetching before it enters context (cross-ref cost), and measure attribution directly rather than assuming a fluent answer is a grounded one.

themes.title: Picking the retrieval architecture: SQL, graph, gateway, or managed service
themes.summary: Teams choose per job between exact SQL, knowledge graphs, self-hosted gateways, and managed search; production wins come from governed data layers more than retrieval tricks.

themes.title: Better retrievers and smarter search effort
themes.summary: Stronger and multimodal embedders, structured chart extraction, learned per-query search depth, and set-sufficiency recovery each raise recall without changing the store.

themes.title: Cutting what retrieval puts into context
themes.summary: Raw fetched pages waste tens of thousands of tokens; pre-compression, reusable compression views, and distraction-resistant models shrink or harden the retrieved context.

themes.title: Evidence that misleads without being false
themes.summary: Truthful but reordered, nearby, or embedding-mimicking evidence redirects agents; defenses normalize presentation or screen documents, and none transfers cleanly yet.

themes.title: Proving the answer is backed by its source
themes.summary: Attribution is now measured and enforced, with citation benchmarks, per-claim source verifiers for MCP agents, pre-execution checks against ground truth, and rule engines that decide while RAG explains.

entries.title: ProvenanceGuard checks per claim that an MCP agent cites the source a fact actually came from
entries.html:
Multi-tool agents can state a true fact but attribute it to the wrong source, for example citing the account record for a fact that lives in the policy document. Pooled faithfulness scores miss this cross-source conflation.

ProvenanceGuard is a post-generation verifier that reads the captured tool trace with source IDs and never pools evidence. It splits the answer into claims, routes each to its likeliest source, checks support, compares that source with the one cited, and emits per-claim verdicts plus an allow/block decision, with no agent retraining.

evidence.title: Getting the Source Right, Not Just the Fact: Source-Aware Verification for MCP Agents

entries.title: ai-rete-rag: a Rete rule engine makes the decision, RAG only explains it
entries.html:
For decisions that must be auditable (lending, fraud, clinical triage), ai-rete-rag runs two systems in series. A pure-Python Rete engine evaluates YAML rules: same facts, same verdict, every time. Then RAG retrieves passages from the organization's policy documents and an LLM writes a plain-English explanation citing them, with no ability to change the verdict.

The explanation cannot drift from what actually decided, the way a model's post-hoc rationale can. See agent reliability.

evidence.title: Show HN: AI·rete·RAG – a Rete rule engine decides, RAG explains why

entries.title: For coding agents, recover a sufficient evidence set, not the top-ranked passages: 73.0% vs 61.4%
entries.html:
A coding agent mid-task has already read much of what a retriever ranks highest, and a ranker can fill its budget with variants of one fact. MSS-Complement conditions on the agent's captured state and uses three semantic calls to propose a jointly sufficient set, find what is missing, and return 4-8 source units within budget.

On SERBench (500 held-out states from 45 repositories) it recovers a complete evidence set 73.0% of the time at five items, versus 61.4% for embedding-based reranking.

evidence.title: The Missing Complement: State-Conditioned Minimal Sufficient Evidence for Coding Agents

entries.title: RAFT retrieves support cases by matching intermediate states, not whole documents
entries.html:
Standard RAG treats historical support cases as static documents. RAFT abstracts each closed case into a directed chain of timeline entries and retrieves at the entry level, surfacing past cases whose intermediate states match the active one and returning the parent case's trajectory.

For troubleshooting agents, the retrieval unit should mirror how the work unfolds. Pick the index structure for the job, as with SQL over embeddings.

evidence.title: RAFT: A Stateful Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Troubleshooting Agents

entries.title: Four knowledge-graph patterns for agentic RAG, including decision provenance
entries.html:
Cassie Shum's InfoQ talk lays out four patterns for building agents on a knowledge graph instead of basic RAG: context bundling, decision provenance, code as truth, and agent visibility. She demonstrates an engineering harness on a graph that shortens feedback loops and reduces token use.

Decision provenance puts attribution into the retrieval architecture itself rather than bolting it on as a separate scoring step.

evidence.title: Presentation: From Retrieval to Reasoning: Building Production-Ready Agentic AI Systems with Knowledge Graphs

entries.title: REVA reuses past attention traces to compress RAG context 5-15x faster than per-query compressors
entries.html:
REVA treats RAG compression as data mining: it aggregates a generator's historical query-document attention into a document-keyed, budget-agnostic score store, then renders plain-text views at any budget while keeping document order and the standard RAG interface.

The authors show existing compressors gain unstably over simple truncation and can add latency. REVA improves quality 1.0-5.8 points over them, cuts compression overhead 5.3x-15.6x, and adds under 40ms.

evidence.title: REVA: Reusable Evidence View Aggregation for Context-Efficient RAG Serving

entries.title: Databricks' Adaptive Instructed-Retriever learns per query how hard to search, at half the latency
entries.html:
Databricks' retriever takes enterprise schemas and custom instructions as input and uses reinforcement learning (CISPO) to decide when one parallel search pass is enough and when a question needs sequential multi-hop search, with search cost in the reward.

It matches Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.6 Luna answer quality at about 5.8s end-to-end, roughly half the latency, and the vendor reports it dominates their quality-vs-cost curves across the retrieval budget. Search effort becomes a learned per-query decision, not a fixed step count.

evidence.title: Adaptive Instructed-Retriever: Frontier-Quality Search at 2x Lower Latency

entries.title: KDDI built its consumer RAG app Buffmee on Google's ADK to balance quality and response time
entries.html:
KDDI, a major Japanese carrier, built Buffmee, a consumer RAG app that grounds answers in over 100 sources including books, magazines, and web media, on Google's Agent Development Kit. The design goal was high generation quality with fast responses across diverse media types.

At consumer scale the quality-versus-latency budget drives the retrieval architecture itself. See agent latency for the serving side.

evidence.title: How KDDI built Buffmee, a faster, reliable consumer RAG app

entries.title: SCoNE makes RAG less distractible by strengthening context-aware neurons, with no fine-tuning
entries.html:
When retrieved documents mix useful and irrelevant context, models get distracted and hallucinate. SCoNE is a training-free edit: it finds context-aware FFN neurons with high attribution and high cross-input variability, then strengthens only those.

It needs a small mining sample, no fine-tuning, and no inference-time overhead, and reports consistent gains over baseline RAG methods on several knowledge-intensive QA benchmarks and two backbones. It applies to self-hosted open-weight models only.

evidence.title: SCoNE: Selective Context-aware Neuron Editing for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

entries.title: Lazy Grounding: true evidence for a nearby question cuts search-agent accuracy up to 17.3 points
entries.html:
Lazy Grounding shows a search agent can be misled without any false document. Using answer-changing rewrites of benchmark questions, each injected document truthfully supports a nearby question but surfaces for the original one, and agents adopt the nearby answer.

Accuracy drops 5.9 points on average and up to 17.3 points across 12 model-benchmark combinations. Fact-checking retrieved text will not catch it; the check has to be whether the evidence answers this question.

evidence.title: Lazy Grounding: Attacking Search Agents with Factual Evidence

entries.title: Cloudflare AI Search runs crawl, parse, embed, and retrieve as one hosted service with an MCP endpoint
entries.html:
Cloudflare AI Search provides a ready-made search engine over custom data: crawl, parse, embed, and retrieve behind one search endpoint, with multimodal search, a "discover" mode that indexes pages without a sitemap, and public /mcp and /search endpoints agents can query directly.

It is the gateway pattern as a managed service: faster setup, less control over chunking, embedding, and ranking than a self-hosted stack.

evidence.title: Cloudflare Extends AI Search to Make it Easier for Agents and Developers to Search Custom Data

entries.title: Tencent's WeMM-Embedding-9B embeds text, images, video, and documents in one space
entries.html:
Tencent released WeMM-Embedding-9B on Hugging Face. Built on Qwen3.5, it embeds text, images, video, and visual documents into one 4,096-dimension space. It scores 80.6 average on MMEB-v2 (78 datasets), ahead of Qwen3-VL-Embedding's 77.8, and 59.5 on the harder MMEB-v3 (190 tasks).

A retriever that natively embeds slide decks and chart-heavy pages can reach multimodal evidence without a separate extraction pass.

evidence.title: tencent/WeMM-Embedding-9B released on Hugging Face

entries.title: Embedding charts as structured JSON beats larger multimodal embedders on chart-heavy retrieval
entries.html:
Databricks parses chart figures into structured JSON with ai_parse_document and embeds that enriched chunk instead of the caption alone, using a 300M-parameter embedding model. On chart-heavy ViDoRe V3 (310 questions) it reaches 75.9% answer correctness from the top-3 retrieved images, and 75.1% on a synthetic Chart-RAG set.

It beats four larger multimodal embedding baselines while passing the agent fewer images: a small model over structured content can out-retrieve a bigger one over raw pixels.

evidence.title: Enhancing Agent Retrieval with Structured Chart Extraction

entries.title: An Evaluation Agent screens retrieved documents for poisoning with NLI checks and a Trust Index
entries.html:
RAG systems trust whatever ranks as relevant, but relevance is not truth. This middleware combines NLI fact-checking, a five-signal poison detector, and a weighted Trust Index (0.4 factuality + 0.35 coherence + 0.25 (1 - poison)) with a dampener for heavily contaminated contexts.

  • On TruthfulQA it reaches 91% accuracy and 100% recall on instruction-injection attempts.
  • In-place edits such as entity swaps stay hard to catch.
  • On FEVER, thresholds need per-model recalibration rather than transferring as-is.

See prompt injection for the attack side.

evidence.title: Trustworthy RAG: An Evaluation Agent for Detecting Misinformation and Knowledge Poisoning in Generative AI Systems

entries.title: DSPrompt defends multimodal RAG against poisoned embeddings that mimic benign entries
entries.html:
In multimodal RAG, attackers craft data whose embeddings align with benign entries in the vector space, so poisoned content is retrieved as if relevant. Existing query-time defenses (auxiliary detectors, similarity re-ranking, consistency checks) add inference overhead and generalize poorly. DSPrompt proposes a dynamic soft-prompt defense instead.

The attack targets the embedding space directly, so retriever ranking alone cannot be trusted as a relevance signal on untrusted corpora.

evidence.title: DSPrompt: Dynamic Soft Prompt Defense Against M-RAG Corruption

entries.title: Sentence Transformers adds off-the-shelf multi-vector (late-interaction) embedding models
entries.html:
Sentence Transformers now supports multi-vector, late-interaction (ColBERT-style) models: a query is matched against several token-level vectors per document instead of one pooled vector.

Self-hosted retrieval stacks get a packaged path to an architecture that was mostly confined to specialized research code. Expect larger indexes in exchange for finer-grained matching.

evidence.title: Multi-Vector (Late Interaction) Embedding Models with Sentence Transformers

entries.title: OneAdvanced self-hosts Llama 4 and a pgvector RAG pipeline for 50+ UK-sovereign agents
entries.html:
OneAdvanced, a UK enterprise software provider, built a UK-sovereign AI platform on AWS: Llama 4 Maverick and Llama Guard 4 self-hosted on SageMaker AI, a RAG pipeline on pgvector, and more than 50 agents built with the Strands Agents SDK on ECS.

Here data residency, not cost or latency, drove the self-hosted retrieval stack, and the model choice and retrieval architecture were decided together.

evidence.title: How OneAdvanced deployed over 50 AI agents on UK-sovereign AWS

entries.title: LangChain's trusted data agent rests on dbt, a semantic layer, and observability, and scaled self-service 40x
entries.html:
LangChain built its internal data agent on Hex, dbt, semantic models, and observability tooling, and reports a 40x increase in self-service analysis.

The governed semantic layer under the agent, not a better retrieval trick on top, is what made answers trustworthy. Grounding a data agent is a data-engineering investment. See agent observability for the tracing side.

evidence.title: How LangChain Built an Agent-First Data Stack

entries.title: AWS TAKC pre-compresses a whole knowledge base into task-specific tiers ahead of query time
entries.html:
AWS describes task-aware knowledge compression (TAKC) for analytical questions that span hundreds of documents, where plain RAG hits a ceiling. It pre-compresses the knowledge base into task-specific representations, caches them at multiple fidelity tiers, and routes each query to the right tier. An open-source implementation is included.

It trades an up-front compression pass for a smaller, denser context at answer time, instead of retrieving and re-reading raw pages per query.

evidence.title: Beyond RAG: Task-aware knowledge compression for enterprise AI on AWS

entries.title: For enterprise data integration, agentic RAG buys accuracy that naive RAG lacks, at a cost to measure
entries.html:
A vision paper on LLM-driven data integration finds naive RAG keeps hitting accuracy and cost limits in enterprise settings because of a persistent knowledge gap. It argues for knowledge-grounded agents in an agentic RAG loop that retrieves, checks, and re-queries, with integration decisions backed by retrieved evidence.

The paper frames agentic RAG as a trade to measure against the naive baseline, not an automatic upgrade: each extra loop buys accuracy with more calls.

evidence.title: Towards Trustworthy and Cost-Efficient Data Integration: From Naïve RAG to Agentic RAG

entries.title: ActionRail checks an agent's proposed action against ground-truth business data before it executes
entries.html:
ActionRail, an open-source framework from ToolJet, adds runtime value and action grounding: before an agent's proposed action or value executes, it is checked against ground-truth business data.

Grounding moves from a retrieval-quality score after the fact to a deployable guard in front of side effects, aimed at the value-poisoning failure benchmarks measure (see agent benchmarks).

evidence.title: Show HN: ActionRail, Runtime value/action grounding framework for AI agents

entries.title: Salience Induction redirects multi-hop RAG agents with only true facts, at 83.3% success
entries.html:
Salience Induction is a third attack channel beyond content poisoning and prompt injection: truth-preserving edits to fact position, emphasis, framing, and semantic proximity redirect a multi-hop agent's reasoning with no false claims and no instructions.

  • Across five model families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen) and ReAct, Reflexion, and tool-calling agents, a 30% edit budget reaches 83.3% attack success.
  • The strongest baseline defense still lets 75.7% through.
  • The authors' Salience Normalization cuts it to 15.3% (23.6% under adaptive attacks).

Content filters will not catch this; the defense has to normalize how evidence is presented.

evidence.title: Salience Induction against Multi-Hop RAG Agents: Threat and Defense

entries.title: OpenWiki 0.2 adopts OKF so agents can filter codebase docs by metadata instead of searching
entries.html:
OpenWiki 0.2 generates codebase wikis in OKF, a proposed open format that adds YAML front matter (tags, categories, timestamps), changelogs, and directory index files to doc pages.

An agent can filter to "every doc tagged billing" directly instead of running an open-ended search. It is the structured-recall argument applied to the docs coding agents ground their answers on.

evidence.title: OpenWiki 0.2 brings OKF to codebase documentation

entries.title: Postgres for agents: assemble context with plain SQL first, vectors only for the fuzzy slice
entries.html:
Gwen Shapira's InfoQ talk shows teams delivering deterministic and semantic context from one Postgres: JSONB and plain SQL for what can be looked up exactly ("how would a human solve this?"), HNSW vector indexing for genuinely fuzzy matches, and vector quantization for roughly 4x faster queries.

Deterministic retrieval is a live alternative to embedding everything. Reach for similarity search only when an exact query cannot express the question.

evidence.title: Presentation: Postgres for Production Agents: Your Relational Foundation for Enterprise AI

entries.title: Orbit packages file RAG, multi-backend vector RAG, and NL-to-query into one self-hosted gateway
entries.html:
Orbit is an open-source toolkit for retrieval-based inference that bundles file RAG, vector RAG across Chroma, Qdrant, Pinecone, Weaviate, pgvector, and FAISS, and natural-language-to-query translation over SQL, NoSQL, and REST sources.

"Which store, which query language" becomes a routing decision inside one gateway instead of a separate integration per source. That is the build-it-yourself end of the gateway pattern.

evidence.title: Orbit, an Open-Source Toolkit for Retrieval-Based Inference

entries.title: TALRanker decides per document when reranking should call a search tool
entries.html:
The Tool-Adaptive LLM Reranker (TALRanker) targets hallucinated relevance judgments on queries beyond the model's own knowledge. Calling a search tool for every document during reranking fixes accuracy but adds prohibitive latency, so TALRanker frames pointwise relevance scoring as an agentic decision process that invokes external tools only where needed.

It adds a middle option to the rerank stage between a purely parametric reranker and a tool call per candidate.

evidence.title: Tool-Adaptive LLM Reranker

also.title: External knowledge base: vector and graph retrieval

entries.title: ResearchQA scores whether answers are backed by verifiable citations, not just correct
entries.html:
ResearchQA is a benchmark of 6,211 question-answer pairs from 494 open-access papers across eight domains and four question types (lookup, comprehension, multi-hop, adversarial). It allows multiple valid supporting passages per claim and rewards grounded refusal when the paper does not support an answer.

"Grounded or just fluent" becomes a measured number instead of a spot-check, and declining to answer counts as a correct outcome when the evidence is missing.

evidence.title: ResearchQA: Benchmarking Citation-Grounded Question-Answering on Scientific Papers

also.title: External knowledge base: vector and graph retrieval

entries.title: A raw Wikipedia page costs an agent 68,240 tokens before it can ground on anything
entries.html:
A Claude Code user measured page costs: an average Wikipedia article is 68,240 tokens of raw HTML and Nike's homepage 353,000. Claude Code's WebFetch summarizes Wikipedia to about 950 tokens, but returns nothing on JS-rendered and some anti-bot pages, and the agent then dumps raw HTML into context. A stealth-browser fetch tool that converts to markdown brings the page to roughly 3,000-5,000 tokens.

Most of the raw page is boilerplate the model must read before reaching the relevant part. Budget the fetch layer, not just the model call. See agent cost.

evidence.title: One Wikipedia page costs your AI agent 68,000 tokens
